newsitem.title: INDIA: Old campaigners to help mark India independence.
newsitem.headline: Old campaigners to help mark India independence.

text.p: Old fighters will lead thousands in a march, parliament will hold a midnight session and rare Greek and British art objects will be on show as India celebrates its 50 years of independence.

Officials told a news conference on Monday that the year-long celebrations of India's freedom at midnight on August 15, 1947 will start with a celebration in Bombay on August 9 to mark the launch in 1942 of the "Quit India" movement against British rule.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral chaired a meeting on Monday of a committee for the commemoration of the 50th anniversary, comprising independence fighters -- many now in their 70s or older -- political leaders, movie moguls and industrialists.
"I think the most important thing we need to keep in mind is how to inculcate the spirit of patriotism and pride in national movement in the new generation,..." he said.

"Around 340 pieces of art and artefacts (of Greek culture) will be shown for the first time in Asia," Culture Secretary B.P. Singh said, adding the two-month-long show from August 16 would be Greek civilisation's tribute to Indian civilisation.

From October 14, rare British art will be on show for two months in an exhibition expected to coincide with a visit by Queen Elizabeth, who as imperial Britain's Princess announced India's independence in New Delhi in 1947.

At 11.55 p.m. (0625 GMT) on August 14, the president and prime minister of India will lead a special session of parliament to mark the midnight announcement. K.R. Narayanan is scheduled to take office as India's 10th president later this month.
The high point of the session would be the playing of recorded speeches made 50 years ago by independence leader Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru, the first prime minister.

Three hours before midnight on New Delhi's Rajpath boulevard, once called Kingsway, independence fighters will lead a "March of the Nation" featuring floats marking the high points of the freedom movement in front of large video screens.
Parades, fireworks and laser light shows are also planned in New Delhi, where power-starved authorities will loosen regulations to help the illumination of buildings and monuments.
"Every district will have its own calendar of events," Singh said. "A large number of freedom fighters from abroad who had supported India's case are being invited."

The small French-ruled enclave of Pondicherry, which joined India in 1954, plans to celebrate its merger day on October 19. Portuguese-ruled Goa, which joined India in 1961 after an army conquest, proposes to mark December 19 as its "Liberation Day".

There is also a proposal to mark August 11, the day in 1952 when Kashmir's constituent assembly voted to be in the Indian Union, officials said. Neighbouring Pakistan disputes Kashmir, over which it has fought two wars with India.
State-run television has commissioned special series from Indian movie makers for part of 1,200 hours of programmes marking the 50th anniversary of independence, the government said in a statement.
The Finance Ministry will release special coins with the motif of the Dandi March, a protest movement that Gandhi led against a salt tax levied by the British rulers in 1930, it said.
The state-run Minerals and Metals Trading Corp will release gold coins carrying the logo of the 50th anniversary celebrations in the 930-million-strong nation, the world's largest democracy.
